readback.name: Poincare.HamiltonScalarGradientAuxiliaryEstimate.auxiliary_evolution_le_cubic_of_normalizedFlow
readback.mathematical_statement: For every Hausdorff charted space M modeled on real Euclidean three-space with a smooth boundaryless manifold structure given explicitly by modelWithCornersSelf over the real field on that Euclidean space and smooth exponent ((top : ENat) : WithTop ENat), assume M is compact, connected, second countable, and has a measurable structure satisfying BorelSpace. Let gt be any family indexed by all real times of smooth Riemannian metrics. Fix a real time t, a point x in M, and a real eta >= 0. Assume every anchored metric entry is jointly C5 in time and chart coordinates at every (s,y); assume IsClosedNormalizedRicciFlowSolutionAt gt t y for every y; assume scalar curvature at time t is strictly positive at every y; and assume the pinching quotient at x at time t is at most 1. The last quotient is N/R squared, where R is scalar curvature and N is the trace of the squared Ricci endomorphism, so the hypothesis is N <= R squared at this one point. The flow predicate includes Levi-Civita compatibility at each y for every time and the section-tested equation at t of minus twice Ricci plus (2/3) mean scalar times metric. Put R_s(y) = scalar curvature of gt s, S_s(y) = squared norm of grad R_s, U_s(y) = squared traceless Ricci norm = N_s(y) - R_s(y) squared/3, K = 84 + 60 eta, and F(s,y) = S_s(y)/R_s(y) - eta R_s(y) squared + K U_s(y). Let r_t be scalar curvature integrated against Riemannian volume divided by total real volume. Then the ordinary time derivative of F(s,x) at t minus the gt t metric-trace Hessian Laplacian of F(t,.) at x plus (4/3) r_t F(t,x) is at most -(4/3) eta R_t(x) cubed + 4 K R_t(x) U_t(x). The coefficient K cancels the derivative-energy terms because (8 - 2 K/21) A + 2 eta S <= 0 when S <= (20/7) A, and the scalar-square equation contributes -4 eta R N, which is at most -(4/3) eta R cubed since R>0 and U>=0. The cubic traceless-Ricci reaction is controlled by 4 R U using the stated local pinching quotient. Thus the coefficients and the retained normalized term are consistent with the literal assertion. Eta need not be strictly positive; the pinching bound need not hold at other points or times; joint C5 holds at all times but scalar positivity and the flow equation are only required at the selected slice. No positive-Ricci or simply-connectedness hypothesis appears, and F is not asserted nonnegative. This is a pointwise auxiliary differential inequality for an already supplied metric family, not a flow-existence theorem, uniform constant bound on the unadjusted heat operator, maximum-principle conclusion, scalar-gradient decay theorem, convergence theorem, or Poincare proof. The variable normalized zero-order term remains on the left; dropping it would require further sign or comparison information. Approval is for the mathematical assertion and coefficients, not compiler acceptance of an implementation.
